column3: The Hebrew calls the tests riddles; BSB uses “difficult questions.”
The Hebrew retains the heart image; BSB uses “on her mind.”
The Hebrew says all her words and nothing hidden from the king; BSB has questions and nothing too difficult.
The Hebrew calls the building the house; BSB uses palace.
The Hebrew names sitting and standing and has singular burnt offering; BSB has seating, service, and plural offerings. The Hebrew says no spirit remained in her.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes her eyes the subject of seeing and expresses adding wisdom and good as Solomon’s action; BSB has seeing with her eyes and the qualities exceeding the report.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name rather than an explicit pronoun for the one making him king.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly describes the wood as very much; BSB uses “a great cargo.”
The Hebrew uses separate negative coming and being seen clauses; BSB adds “before” with the first.
The Hebrew repeats King Solomon’s name and retains his hand image; BSB uses “his royal bounty.”
The Hebrew says one year; BSB says each year.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has no separate weight unit after six hundred; BSB supplies shekels.
The Hebrew does not separately repeat a making verb; BSB supplies “He also made.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says two lions beside the armrests; BSB distributes these as one beside each.
The Hebrew says on this side and that side; BSB makes one at each end of each step explicit.
The Hebrew has no explicit causal conjunction before silver being considered nothing; BSB uses “because.”
The Hebrew calls the vessels a Tarshish fleet collectively; BSB has plural ships of Tarshish.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains Solomon’s face as the object sought; BSB uses an audience with him.
The Hebrew says each brought his offering, without explicitly calling him a visitor, and repeats the year.
The Hebrew names twelve thousand horsemen; BSB has horses. It explicitly repeats the king where BSB uses “him.”
The Hebrew repeats the giving verb and names abundance with the cedars and sycamores.
The Hebrew explicitly mentions a price in the purchase; BSB leaves this implicit.
The Hebrew retains their hand and has no explicit weight unit after six hundred; BSB supplies shekels.
